svg.aria-label: What to Measure for an AI Service showing availability, latency, cost and quality signals side by side, and which failures each one can and cannot see
svg.title: What to Measure for an AI Service
svg.text: What to Measure for an AI Service
Four families. Each catches failures the others cannot, which is why three of them are not enough.
Availability — error rate
Catches: things that break loudly. 500s, timeouts, crashes.
Cannot see: a request that returns 200 with an invented answer.
This is the only signal most first deployments have.
Latency — percentiles, never the mean
Catches: degradation users feel. Use p95 or p99.
Cannot see: events rarer than 1 - p. Over 20 samples, p95 is
the 19th value — one slow request sits above it, invisible.
Cost — spend per window vs a baseline
Catches: a change that doubles context length; abuse; a leaked key.
Cannot see: anything, if compared to a FIXED cap — which either
never fires or always does. Normal varies, so compare to normal.
Quality — did the answer cite anything?
Catches: the failure unique to AI systems.
These requests SUCCEED. 200 OK, fast, cheap, and the index is
empty so every answer is confidently invented.
The window that makes the case
Measured in the lab: err=0%, p95=1311ms, spend normal — and 40% of answers cited nothing at all. Availability,
latency and cost were all green while the system returned fluent, ungrounded text to nearly half its users.
A groundedness flag on each request costs almost nothing to record, and it is the only signal that sees this.
